newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INZAGHI THE LONER IN FAMILIAR ITALY SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INZAGHI THE LONER IN FAMILIAR ITALY SQUAD.

text.p: Atalanta's Filippo Inzaghi, leading goalscorer in serie A, stood out on Monday in an injury-depleted but predictable Italian squad for the World Cup qualifier against Poland on April 30.

Inzaghi, whose winner for Atalanta in a 1-0 victory against Napoli in Naples on Sunday night was his 19th goal of the season, was the only player in a 19-man squad still waiting for his senior international baptism.
He had been called up for the previous two World Cup qualifiers but failed to get a game.

Coach Cesare Maldini stuck with familiar faces, summoning an unchanged squad from the one called up for matches in late March and early April against Moldova in Trieste and an away trip to Poland -- minus three injured players.
The missing three were Lazio defender Alessandro Nesta, injured against Moldova when Italy won 3-0, Juventus striker Michele Padovano and Parma attacker Enrico Chiesa. They were not replaced.

Padovano and striker Christian Vieri were both uncapped before those matches but got a look-in over Inzaghi, with Vieri -- like Inzaghi a stalwart of Maldini's under-21 team -- marking his debut with Italy's 1,000th international goal.
Juventus attacker Alessandro Del Piero, recovering from a muscle injury, was not included either.

Middlesbrough's Fabrizio Ravanelli, who missed the last two World Cup qualifiers due to injury, returns -- assuming he makes it safely through a tiring week in England with an F.A. Cup semifinal replay on Tuesday and league match on Thursday.

If Inzaghi may not be the flavour of the night for the Neapolitan crowd after consigning their serie A team towards the relegation zone, Juventus's Naples-born defender Ferrara may expect a better reception than his last visit.

Ferrara, who helped Napoli to two league titles in 1987 and 1990, was booed and whistled by the crowd every time he touched the ball at the San Paolo stadium on March 23 when Juventus drew 0-0 with Napoli.
Some fans had not forgiven him for joining Juventus after 11 seasons at the southern club.
Italy lead group two after four wins and a draw and have yet to concede a goal under Maldini's leadership.
Defenders - Ciro Ferrara (Juventus), Alessandro Costacurta (Milan), Fabio Cannavaro (Parma), Paolo Maldini (Milan), Antonio Benarrivo (Parma), Christian Panucci (Real Madrid, Spain)
Midfielders - Angelo Di Livio (Juventus), Roberto Di Matteo (Chelsea, England), Demetrio Albertini (Milan), Dino Baggio (Parma), Diego Fuser (Lazio), Amedeo Carboni (Roma), Stefano Eranio (Milan)
Strikers - Christian Vieri (Juventus), Filippo Inzaghi (Atalanta), Fabrizio Ravanelli (Middlesbrough, England), Gianfranco Zola (Chelsea, England)
